claims.statement: The pinned migration fragment says scripts and Actions workflows using the Docker registry namespace continue working after Container Registry migration. Resolved namespaces are docker.pkg.github.com to ghcr.io for FPT/GHEC and docker.HOSTNAME to containers.HOSTNAME for GHES. Compatibility is a source claim, not a completed migration or tested consumer receipt.

The upstream fragment identifies Container Registry as replacing GitHub's Docker registry; this does not authorize migration or establish a particular target's enabled service or present lifecycle status.

The npm configuration step places .npmrc alongside package.json and sets a namespace-specific registry. The packages-npm-v2 feature, FPT/GHEC in the pin, scopes the namespace to a user or organization account; other contexts use the owning repository account. FPT/GHEC endpoint is npm.pkg.github.com; enterprise endpoints depend on subdomain isolation, npm.HOSTNAME versus HOSTNAME/_registry/npm. Placeholders require verified target values; no configuration or credentials were written.

The default publication association is an existing repository sharing the package name. This fragment alone does not define every registry's association model, demonstrate a real publication or authorize creating or changing repositories.

Deleting an account deletes its namespace's Packages packages and container images and may break dependent projects. For FPT/GHEC public container images with strictly more than 5,000 downloads, the full namespace/image name is permanently retired on account deletion. This conditional consequence is not universal name retirement, a >= threshold, deletion approval or a recovery guarantee.

Actions workflow REST package deletion and restoration are described as public preview and subject to change; the beta filename does not override the release-phase variable. This note does not supply permissions, executed behavior or mutation approval.
